Step 1: Identify that triangle \(ABD\), \(BCD\), and \(ACD\) are all isosceles triangles because \(AD = BD = CD\).

Step 2: Let \(\angle BAC = x\). Since \(AD = BD\), \(\angle ADB = \angle BAD = x\).

Step 3: Because \(AD = CD\), \(\angle CAD = \angle ACD\). Let \(\angle CAD = \angle ACD = y\).

Step 4: The sum of angles in triangle \(ABC\) is \(180^\circ\). Therefore, \(\angle ABC + \angle BCA + \angle BAC = 180^\circ\

Step 5: Since \(\angle BCA = 40^\circ\), we have \(\angle ABC + 40^\circ + x = 180^\circ\).

Step 6: In \(\triangle ABD\), the angles sum to \(180^\circ\), so \(x + x + \angle ADB = 180^\circ\). This simplifies to \(2x + \angle ADB = 180^\circ\).

Step 7: In \(\triangle ACD\), the angles also sum to \(180^\circ\), so \(y + y + \angle ACD = 180^\circ\). This simplifies to \(2y + \angle ACD = 180^\circ\).

Step 8: Note that \(\angle ADB = \angle ACD\) because they are vertical angles. Let \(\angle ADB = \angle ACD = z\).

Step 9: From Step 6, \(2x + z = 180^\circ\).

Step 10: From Step 7, \(2y + z = 180^\circ\).

Step 11: Since \(\angle ABC = 180^\circ - 40^\circ - x = 140^\circ - x\), and \(\angle ABC = 2y\) (from the exterior angle theorem applied to \(\triangle ACD\)), we get \(2y = 140^\circ - x\).

Step 12: Substitute \(z = 180^\circ - 2x\) from Step 9 into the equation for \(\angle ACD\) in Step 7, giving \(2y + 180^\circ - 2x = 180^\circ\). Simplifying, we get \(2y = 2x\), or \(y = x\).

Step 13: Substitute \(y = x\) into \(2y = 140^\circ - x\) from Step 11, giving \(2x = 140^\circ - x\). Solving for \(x\), we get \(3x = 140^\circ\), so \(x = \frac{140^\circ}{3} = 46.67^\circ\).

Final answer: \boxed{46.67}
